text:
maria: Heads up — after today's canary (v0.78.3) we're seeing a sustained token/sec drop on CTB for low-seqlen workloads, ~30-40% on average :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy v0.78.3 to canary completed (build 2026-03-18_09:22) :white_check_mark:

kevin: Yep I saw that in the dashboard. Latency p50 is fine but tokens/sec and tail latency slipped. KV cache hit-rate down ~12% on microbench job.

olivia: Any obvious diff in kernel selection or batch composition? Could be the new kernel-affinity heuristic we merged this morning.

sanjay: I pulled a flamegraph from the canary yesterday vs pre-release — CPU/GPU scheduling shows more time in memcopy and small-kernel dispatch overhead. KV miss spiky right after coalescing.

maria: Paste profiling outputs? small snippet is fine.

sanjay: Here — microprofile on a 32k request set (small seq):
```
pre-release: kv_hit=0.89, avg_batch=6.2, tokens/sec=9800
canary:      kv_hit=0.77, avg_batch=5.9, tokens/sec=6100
kernel-path: pre used fp16-small-batched kernel, canary chose unified-kernel v2 (more memcpy)
```

kevin: I bisected locally to commit abc1234 (PR #4127) — the change that shifted kernel affinity to prefer the unified path when batch_size < 8 to avoid a slow codepath in the old fp16 kernel. That heuristic looks reversed for our small-seqlen traffic.

ben: CI perf job picked up a regression last night but it wasn't blocking. I flagged it as "investigate"; looks like it blew up after this morning's merge. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/98765

olivia: For immediate mitigation I'd recommend rollout hold on canary and revert abc1234. We can follow up with a tuned heuristic that takes kv_hit into account.

maria: Agreed — hold canary, don't promote. Can ops put rollout hold? :hand:

deploy-bot: Rollout hold applied to v0.78.3 canary by olivia at 09:29 UTC.

kevin: I'll open a revert PR now and add a test that simulates high small-seqlen mix + low kv hit to ensure we don't flip affinity incorrectly.

sanjay: Also adding a perf regression test for token/sec against microbench harness would help catch this earlier.

maria: Plan: 1) kevin revert PR -> run perf CI with microbench 2) if green, hotfix canary -> validate KV hit + tokens/sec 3) roll forward with a new heuristic PR that factors kv_hit and memcopy cost.

olivia: I'll add a dashboard alert if kv_hit drops >6% within a 10m window so we catch next ones faster.

ben: FYI I'll mark the earlier CI failure as correlated to the merge and escalate if perf CI fails on the revert.

maria: Thanks all. Keep updates in this thread. If anyone finds a quick kernel patch that costs less memcpy instead of full revert call it out.

kevin: Revert PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4150 — running perf CI now.

deploy-bot: perf CI started for PR 4150 (microbench-suite).

maria: :rocket:
